body.statement: Under the hypotheses of \(\mathrm{lem:graphical\mbox{-}replacement\mbox{-}preservation}\), there exist finite-alphabet local kernels \(\widetilde\kappa=(\widetilde\kappa_v^{(j)})_{v\in V\cup S,\ 0\le j\le K}\) factoring over the basal DAG in \(\operatorname{RepGraph}(\eta,B)\), satisfying \(\widetilde\kappa_v^{(k)}=\widetilde\kappa_v^{(0)}\) for every \(v\notin\widetilde T_k\), and assigning positive probability to \(S^*=\mathbf 1\), such that the resulting fully specified model \(\widetilde\eta\) belongs to \(\operatorname{Real}(\eta,B)\). Simultaneously for every \(k\in[K]\), the selected pooled law \(P_{\widetilde\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) is faithful to \(M_k(\widetilde\eta)\). The kernels \(\widetilde\kappa\) are constructed jointly across regimes and need not equal \(\kappa(\eta)\).
body.justification: A genuine joint kernel construction, rather than graph preservation alone, is required to prove that the replacement specification has a faithful Dai-class realization.
body.gap: Generic single-DAG faithfulness does not by itself produce one family of selected arm laws whose pooled indicator laws are simultaneously faithful to all replacement regime MAGs.
body.consumer: It turns each graphical endpoint modification into a statistically well-defined whole-family witness.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove that the shared finite-alphabet parameter space for every admissible replacement contains kernels whose selected pooled laws are simultaneously faithful to all \(M_k\).
obligation.obstruction: Faithfulness is imposed on members already in \(\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\), but no frozen assumption or cited theorem makes an arbitrary replacement specification a member. Ordinary generic faithfulness for one unconstrained DAG does not cover the common baseline-kernel equalities, conditioning on \(S^*=\mathbf 1\), and all pooled indicator laws at once.
obligation.attempted: Parameterize all positive conditional-probability tables and clear the selection denominators in each conditional-independence determinant. This reduces simultaneous unfaithfulness to a finite union of algebraic zero sets, but closure still requires a nonvanishing witness for every \(m\)-connected query on the shared-parameter subspace. That witness was not derived from the frozen primitives.
obligation.partial_result: For any fixed replacement specification, strictly positive finite conditional-probability tables can be chosen to factor over \(\widetilde G_0\), the same baseline table can be reused at every non-target vertex, and every selection kernel can be made strictly positive; these choices give Markov factorization, non-target kernel stability, and \(\Pr(S^*=\mathbf 1)>0\).  The graphical replacement lemma already proves the desired projected skeletons and unshielded colliders.  What remains unproved is that the shared-parameter space contains a point at which, simultaneously for every \(k\), conditioning on \(S^*=\mathbf 1\) and pooling the two arms with \(\zeta_k\) introduce no conditional independence beyond the \(m\)-separations of \(M_k(\widetilde\eta)\).
